Lina G.: Quick Q  planning holiday travel: if I end the year with ~56h PTO, how much can I carry to next year? Is there any allowance if I have an approved business travel conflict in Jan?
Marco (People Ops): Hi Lina  standard carryover cap for FT is 40 hours. Anything above that expires unless you get an exception. If you have a documented business conflict that prevents you using PTO by Mar 31, we can consider one-time extensions on a case-by-case basis (needs manager note + email to people-ops).
Sasha T.: Can managers pre-approve carryover during year-end reviews to avoid last-minute paperwork?
Marco (People Ops): Managers can signal intent in the headcount/people review, but formal exceptions must be emailed to people-ops with subject line: "PTO Carryover Exception  <Name>" including reason, hours requested, and manager sign-off. We then update Rippling manually.
Lina G.: What about blackout dates? My team plans a release Dec 21-23  are those hard no-PTO days?
Marco (People Ops): We have a soft blackout Dec 20Jan 2 for cross-org coverage. Soft = coordinate with manager; not an absolute ban. Some core roles (infra, support) will have mandatory coverage windows and managers will notify individuals by Nov 15 if on rota.
Sasha T.: If someone is on approved parental leave and ends up with >40h, any special process?
Marco (People Ops): Parents returning from approved parental leave can request a one-time extension, usually granted up to June 30. Send email with manager note and leave dates.
